key_insight: GBClaw links agentic AI workflows with atomistic simulations to reveal how defect hierarchies and metastable structures influence grain-boundary sliding resistance.
engineering_relevance: Understanding grain-boundary deformation mechanisms can inform efforts to control interfacial strength in polycrystalline materials.
method: Coordinate LLM-based specialized agents through an orchestrator, domain tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory.
Dynamically replan simulations and mechanistic analyses as results emerge.
Compare sliding with and without secondary grain-boundary misfit dislocations, then investigate anomalies through researcher-guided calculations.
evidence_signal: Across 14 general asymmetric tilt grain boundaries in nickel, GBClaw identified diverse deformation modes and substantial shear-strength differences associated with secondary misfit dislocations.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the studied nickel boundaries, and resolving an anomalously high shear resistance required researcher-guided follow-up.
paper_title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
